distribution.blocker: No public submission path exists. Audited 2026-08-27: the MCP documentation describes installing from the marketplace, adding anything missing by hand-editing `mcp_config.json`, and deep-linking an existing listing via `windsurf://windsurf-mcp-registry?serverName=`, but it documents no form, PR target, or intake URL by which a third party gets listed. Listings carrying a blue check are described as made by the parent service company, with no path given to obtain one. Blocked on the absence of a channel, not on a queue — so this is not a to-do, and there is nothing to wait for either. Two adjacent facts worth keeping: the windsurf.com docs now 307-redirect to `docs.devin.ai/desktop/...`, so this host ships as Devin Desktop and the old `codeium.com/windsurf` source is stale; and enterprise teams may point Cascade at a custom registry that must follow the official MCP registry schema, which CallLint is already published to. That makes this host reachable per-team through a registry we already satisfy, which is a different mechanism from a public listing and is why the row stays blocked rather than pending.

distribution.blocker: There is nothing to submit, and that is the audit's finding rather than an obstacle. Audited 2026-08-27. Qwen Code publishes no gallery or catalogue of its own; it installs FROM other hosts' shelves and converts on the way in — `qwen extensions install <marketplace>:<plugin>` reads a Claude Code marketplace and converts the Claude manifest to `qwen-extension.json`, translating agents, skills and tool mappings, while `qwen extensions install <owner>/<repo>` does the same for a Gemini extension, carrying MCP servers and context files across. `/extensions explore` browses the Gemini CLI and Claude Code galleries. So this row is derivative of shelves we already publish or are working toward, and submitting to it is not a thing a person can do. Deliberately NOT marked available: no probe has installed CallLint through Qwen, so reachability is inferred from the documented conversion rather than observed, and ADR 0007 admits only observed acts as evidence. What would settle it is one command on a machine with Qwen Code — `qwen extensions install calllint/calllint` — after which this becomes an evidence-backed availability claim rather than a blocked row. Kept out of the to-do list because the to-do list is for acts a human can perform on a channel, and this channel accepts none.

distribution.blocker: Blocked on a licence term, not on a missing channel — and the distinction is the point, because the mechanism here is real and one command long. Audited 2026-08-27. ClawHub hosts exactly three surfaces: Skills (a folder carrying `SKILL.md`), code plugins, and bundle plugins. It hosts no MCP servers, so the obvious reading of this row — publish the MCP server — has no target. But we already ship `skills/secure-agent-install/SKILL.md`, and `clawhub skill publish <path>` takes precisely that, with `--dry-run` first, so no new artifact would be needed. What stops it: publishing a skill to ClawHub releases it under `MIT-0`, and this repository is Apache-2.0. MIT-0 drops the attribution requirement and carries no patent grant, so the act would relicense a shipped artifact on strictly weaker terms than the repo it came from. That is an owner's decision about intellectual property, not an engineering step, and it cannot be inferred from the instruction to submit to shelves — so it is recorded here rather than performed. It also needs `clawhub login` (browser OAuth, `--device`, or a `clh_` token), which is an account only the owner has. DECIDED 2026-08-27: the owner declined, so this is settled rather than pending a decision. The alternative was checked before recording rather than assumed away, and it does not exist — ClawHub's skill format documents no `license` field and states in as many words that it `does not support per-skill license overrides`, with `All skills published on ClawHub are licensed under MIT-0`. So there is no way to list the skill on Apache-2.0 terms, and the channel is closed on a term we will not accept. Not a to-do and not a queue: nobody is reviewing anything, and re-running the audit will reach this same sentence. Two things that would reopen it, neither of which is work we can do: ClawHub adds a per-skill licence field, or it gains a surface that accepts what we actually ship. One route was deliberately left unexplored rather than silently dismissed — ClawHub also hosts code plugins, whose licence terms are documented separately from skills, but reaching it would mean building an OpenClaw plugin against their SDK with `openclaw.compat.pluginApi` and `openclaw.build.openclawVersion`, which is a new artifact and a new maintenance surface, not a submission. If that is ever wanted it should be decided on its own merits, not adopted as a workaround for a licence term.

distribution.blocker: GitHub Copilot CLI does not consume the Official MCP Registry, so there is no registry-discovery channel to submit to. Measured 2026-08-27 on copilot 1.0.80: `copilot mcp add` takes a command or URL with no registry lookup and no name resolution, `copilot mcp list/get` expose no search or discovery flag, and the string `registry.modelcontextprotocol.io` does not appear anywhere in the shipped platform binary — against a positive control on the same search, which finds `mcp-config.json` in that same app.js. Config is loaded only from the user file, the workspace file, or an installed plugin. This row previously carried `upstream: officialMcpRegistry`, which was a claim about a mechanism that does not exist; it is removed rather than left under a pending label, because `upstream` is the evidence arm HD-07 accepts from a channel claiming to be available to users.

calllintSupport.label: Auto-detects
calllintSupport.coverageBoundary: CallLint auto-discovers both Cline config files: the CLI's (~/.cline/data/settings/, relocatable via CLINE_DATA_DIR) and the VS Code extension's, which lives in per-extension globalStorage and is documented by no upstream page. Neither Cline's rules, hooks, skills, agents nor plugins directories are read, and ~/Documents/Cline/MCP/ holds installed server source rather than server registrations, so it is not a config path.

Its MCP servers are plugin instances in cordis.yml rather than an mcpServers map, so no existing extractor reads that shape. This record exists for discovery routing only: DeepSeek is a model vendor here, not a security-relevant distinction.
